Use this process-card rehearsal to learn the sequence. Practical criteria require individual supervision and a real observation of your own performance.
Mixed starting condition
Early sand observation · about1–2minutes
Later silt observation · about2–4hours
Final clay observation · about24–48hours
Unclear boundary · record uncertainty
Sand · bottom
Silt · middle
Clay · upper mineral layer
Floating organic debris · excluded
Source-card order fits. Actual materials, safe shaking and individual performance still need the trainer’s observation.
Matches this teaching timetable only. Record real start and observation times on the same jars; no online wait counts as a physical observation.

sourceBindings.text: One-litre lidded glass jar, approximately half soil, water to about three-quarters, about 1 teaspoon dishwashing liquid, vigorous shaking 10–15 minutes; then a separate pre-settled 48-hour jar for measurement. These are source-card conditions, not an automatically safe or standardized site SOP.
Jar about half full with source soil
Water to about three-quarters full
Approx. 1 tsp stated dishwashing liquid
Lid secured
Vigorous shaking at least 10 minutes
Stable level undisturbed placement
Total mineral layer height measured in mm on pre-settled jar
Sand layer measured in mm
Silt layer measured in mm
Clay layer measured in mm
Sand, silt and clay percentages calculated
Percentages recorded clearly

The trainer checks physical rows 1–6 on each learner's real preparation and later boundaries on the same jars; rows 7–12 are taught and assessed in S2-12. A pre-settled demonstration jar cannot supply personal settling-performance evidence.

The source also lists about1.5cups for a1-litre jar and separately says half full. These are retained as source descriptions, not asserted equal volumes; the trainer documents an actual measure and cup definition. No conversion is invented.

sourceBindings.text: Learner gives USDA fine-earth ranges sand 0.05–2 mm, silt 0.002–0.05 mm, clay <0.002 mm, explains dispersion and settling order, and distinguishes a height-based classroom estimate from a laboratory weight-percentage determination.
Pass with correct sizes and limitations. Particle weight alone, without size, density, aggregation and dispersal, is not a sufficient explanation.

Trainer checks each student's three sample IDs, safe approved vessel and lid, prepared material, documented soil/water/dispersant quantities, mixing, shaking and start time. The source process-card amounts are used only when the trainer explicitly selects that classroom protocol and material.
All critical rows for each jar must be observed or validly repeated. Watching a teammate or using a pre-settled jar cannot replace this preparation.

Trainer records actual timed sand, silt and final clay observations on the learner's own three jars, with any blurred interface or disturbance flagged. Settling may require 24–48 hours, so evidence is collected in separate scheduled stages.
Pass only after the real later observations are documented and reviewed. A 15–20-minute class view or trainer's pre-settled jar is not a final result.
